alignments.note: Passive participle predicate takes the construction-supplied copula, headed on the word carrying the lexeme (rules 20, 24).

Verb with its auxiliary, and with the supplied *without* by which the recast English verb reaches גֹּאֵל: that noun is the bare direct object of הִשְׁבִּית in the Hebrew — no marker and no preposition on it — so rule 44's supplied-preposition clause governs and the word joins the verb's unit, exactly as `טָחוּ תָּפֵל` → *have daubed ... with untempered mortar* does. Rule 33 defers here in its own terms, running the direct-object question first and noting that a recasting which makes a transitive Hebrew verb intransitive always leaves the translator a relation to choose. Unit discontinuous around the negative and around *thee this day* (rule 25). Giving *without* to גֹּאֵל under rule 33's adverbial-accusative sentence was the competing reading, but that sentence reaches a nominal no verb governs.
The לְ is recast as a bare English object *thee* (rule 40).

גֹּאֵל → *a near kinsman*: the indefinite article belongs to the noun that licenses it (rule 15) and the head stays on the class noun, *near* being the ASV's specifier (rule 31). The supplied *without* is the verb's under rule 44, not this noun's.

Niphal קָרָא recast as the volitive *let ... be famous*, headed on the lexical predicate (rule 17); discontinuous around the subject phrase (rule 25). שֵׁם keeps its own *name*, so *famous* is what is left for the verb.

review_notes: Corrected: the supplied *without* moves from גֹּאֵל to the הִשְׁבִּית unit. גֹּאֵל is the bare direct object of that verb in the Hebrew, and rule 33's direct-object paragraph sends such a noun to rule 44's supplied-preposition clause, whatever preposition the ASV chose; the deferral holds because the ASV has itself rendered the governing verb as an English verb, *left*.

The rest of the verse is unchanged: the copula of *Blessed be* is on the participle (rule 20), the לְ of לָךְ is `unrepresented` with its suffix taking *thee* (rule 40), and the article of הַיּוֹם takes the determiner *this* (rule 41).
